raw.text: # E-commerce, products, and food Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## COM-01 — Modular desk lamp hero ```text Create a square catalog photograph of a fictional modular desk lamp. One matte butter-yellow lamp has a cylindrical weighted base, a single hinged arm and a shallow conical shade; place it on an ivory tabletop with a cobalt repair knob beside the base. Use soft light from the upper left and a gentle contact shadow. The only text is "LATCH" on the base and "Keep the light" in the upper-left margin. Preserve plausible joints and one power cord. No certification badges, prices or extra parts. Variables: finish and approved brand text. ``` ## COM-02 — Lunchbox product views ```text Using one authorized product photograph as the geometry reference, create a 16:9 presentation with four equal views of the same rectangular lunchbox: front closed, rear closed, open overhead and latch close-up. Use a pale seamless background and identical soft lighting. Label the views only "Front", "Back", "Inside", and "Latch". Preserve compartment count, seal color and latch placement in every view; invent no dimensions or material claims. Leave visible space between panels. Variables: product reference and translated labels. ``` ## COM-03 — Three tea tins ```text Create a 3:2 packaging concept for three fictional tea tins sharing one cylindrical shape. Arrange them in a straight line, with distinct cream, lavender and sage label bands. Use the shared brand "Field Notes" and the respective names "Morning", "Noon", and "Evening"; add no other text. Photograph on a neutral shelf with consistent highlights and scale. Keep lids, typography alignment and label width identical across all three tins. Do not claim ingredients, origin or health benefits. Variables: approved brand, names and colors. ``` ## COM-04 — Backpack feature board ```text Use an authorized backpack reference and three supplied feature descriptions to create a 3:4 product information image. Place the full backpack on the left; align three detail circles vertically on the right, linked only to the relevant zip, shoulder strap and side pocket. Render exactly [APPROVED FEATURE LABELS] beside their matching circles. Use a pale gray background and controlled studio lighting. Preserve actual construction and colors; no waterproof, capacity or ergonomic claim unless explicitly supplied. Variables: reference, labels and accent color. ``` ## COM-05 — Bread making process ```text Create a 16:9 four-panel image showing one fictional bakery's sourdough workflow: mixing dough, folding dough, scoring a shaped loaf and presenting the baked loaf. Use close documentary photography on the same wooden bench, left-to-right reading order and consistent flour-dusted hands. Label panels "Mix", "Fold", "Score", and "Bake". Keep exactly four panels and distinguish raw dough from baked crust. Do not add cooking temperatures or timing. This is an illustrative process concept, not food-safety instruction. Variables: dough type and approved labels. ``` ## COM-06 — Lunch assortment ```text Create a 16:9 overhead catalog image of four realistic lunch bowls in a two-by-two grid: roasted squash and rice, mushrooms and noodles, lentils and carrots, and tomatoes with couscous. Use identical shallow white bowls, distinct textures, soft daylight and a muted green table. Leave equal gaps and no overlapping utensils. Add no text, calorie counts, dietary guarantees or ingredient labels. Keep plausible portions and avoid repeated food textures. Variables: four supplied recipes, bowl finish and tabletop color. ``` ## COM-07 — Bilingual noodle menu ```text Create a 3:4 menu for fictional café "小巷面馆" with the subtitle "LANE NOODLES". Use ivory paper, charcoal type and three horizontal rows; each row pairs one small realistic bowl photograph on the left with its text on the right. Render exactly "番茄面 · Tomato noodles · 28", "菌菇面 · Mushroom noodles · 32", and "芝麻面 · Sesame noodles · 30". Match red tomato broth, mushroom topping and sesame dressing to their respective rows. No currency symbol, allergens, extra dishes or claims. This is fictional menu copy; retain both languages exactly. ``` ## COM-08 — Room textile comparison ```text Use one authorized room photograph to create a 16:9 two-panel comparison. The left panel reproduces the source; the right changes only the sofa throw and two cushions to [APPROVED COLORS]. Keep windows, walls, furniture positions, camera angle and light unchanged. Label panels "Original" and "Textile concept" in a slim border outside the photographs. Preserve fabric folds and contact shadows; do not repair the room, remove personal belongings or invent extra décor. Variables: source image and colors. ``` ## COM-09 — Refill package instructions ```text Create a 3:4 packaging-use concept with three vertically stacked panels: empty bottle beside refill pouch, pouch nozzle pouring into bottle, and closed bottle next to folded empty pouch. Use the same unbranded amber bottle and ivory pouch in all panels, with clean technical illustration and sage arrows. Render only "Open", "Refill", and "Close". Keep exactly three steps, no liquid spills and no reversed pouring direction. Do not imply food or chemical compatibility. Variables: verified container design and approved instruction labels. ``` ## COM-10 — Bundle contents flat lay ```text Using [APPROVED CONTENTS LIST] and authorized product references, create a square flat lay showing exactly one of each included item in a starter stationery kit. Arrange the notebook centrally and smaller items around it with generous spacing; use warm paper texture and soft overhead light. Add only the title "Inside the kit" and the supplied item names aligned to their objects. Preserve item counts, relative size and colors. Do not add gifts, prices, warranty seals or accessories absent from the list. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

raw.text: # Infographics, education, and business Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## EDU-01 — Rainwater journey ```text Create a 16:9 classroom infographic titled "Where rain goes". Show one house roof, one connected gutter, one covered water barrel and one planted rain garden as four clear stages from left to right. Use blue water arrows from roof to gutter to barrel, then a separate overflow arrow from barrel to garden. Label only "Roof", "Gutter", "Storage", and "Rain garden" beside the correct objects. Use cream background and simple cutaway illustration. Do not show drinking-water use or invent capacity figures. Keep arrows unambiguous and the barrel closed. ``` ## EDU-02 — Urban shade comparison ```text Create a 16:9 teaching diagram comparing two fictional street sections under the same sun angle. The left has no trees; the right has two mature trees shading the sidewalk. Use identical buildings, road width and pedestrians, simple architectural illustration and clear shadow footprints. Label panels "Open sun" and "Tree shade". Add no temperatures, percentages or health outcomes. Keep the sun direction consistent and do not imply that shade removes all heat. Variables: street geometry and approved labels. ``` ## EDU-03 — Seed growth worksheet ```text Create a portrait 3:4 worksheet for children about observing a bean seed. Draw four equally sized boxes containing seed, root emergence, first shoot and two leaves. Leave a ruled observation area beneath each box. Use crisp grayscale line drawings and large lettering. Render only "Watch a seed grow", "1", "2", "3", "4", and "My observations". Keep biological order clear without specifying elapsed days. Do not fill the answer areas or add decorative pseudo-text. Variables: approved plant species and worksheet title. ``` ## EDU-04 — Fraction strip comparison ```text Create a grayscale-friendly 3:4 teaching sheet showing three identical horizontal bars. Divide them into two, four and eight equal segments; shade one, two and four segments respectively. Label the rows "1/2", "2/4", and "4/8"; title the sheet "Same amount, different parts". Align bar beginnings and ends precisely and leave the lower quarter blank for discussion notes. Use clear black outlines and one gray fill. No circles, uneven segments, answer bubbles or additional equations. ``` ## EDU-05 — Monthly service dashboard ```text Create a 16:9 dashboard concept using only [VERIFIED MONTHLY TABLE]. Place the supplied headline metric on the left and a line chart on the right; below, show three labeled supporting figures. Use a white background, charcoal text and one blue series. Render exact dates, units and source note from the table. Preserve missing values as gaps; do not interpolate or invent comparisons. Axes must match supplied scales and show units. Variables: table, metric names, source and period. ``` ## EDU-06 — Three-stage roadmap ```text Create a 16:9 product roadmap using [APPROVED INITIATIVES]. Arrange three equal columns titled "Now", "Next", and "Exploring", with no more than three initiative cards each. Use a clean editorial grid, cream cards and muted blue accents; connect only explicitly supplied dependencies. Include the footer "Planning view, not a release commitment". Do not invent dates, completion status, owners or promises. Keep every initiative in its supplied column. Variables: initiative list and dependency list. ``` ## EDU-07 — Museum route map ```text Use an approved floor plan and [ROOM LABELS] to create a portrait visitor-map concept. Preserve entrances, stairs, lifts, walls and accessible routes exactly; simplify decorative detail only. Highlight one supplied route with a continuous blue line and mark its start and finish. Use a clear legend with supplied symbols and render only approved room names. Do not invent exits, accessibility features or scale. Include "Illustrated guide — verify on site". Variables: plan, route and labels; require venue review before publication. ``` ## EDU-08 — Library service blueprint ```text Create a 16:9 service blueprint for borrowing a library item. Use four columns: "Find", "Reserve", "Collect", "Return"; and three rows: "Reader", "Library", "System". Fill cells only with [APPROVED ACTIONS] and draw arrows only for supplied handoffs. Use restrained blue lines, white cells and large text. Keep customer actions distinct from internal operations. No fabricated turnaround times, personal data or decorative icons replacing actions. Variables: action matrix and verified handoffs. ``` ## EDU-09 — Workshop capacity chart ```text Create a 4:3 information card from this fictional dataset: Monday 8 seats, Tuesday 12 seats, Wednesday 6 seats. Title it "Workshop places available" and draw three horizontal bars on one shared zero-based scale, with exact values at bar ends. Use navy labels and ochre bars on white. Include "Illustrative data" in the footer. Do not convert seats to attendance or percentages, and do not change bar order. Keep the twelve-seat bar twice as long as the six-seat bar. ``` ## EDU-10 — Decision tree teaching card ```text Create a 3:4 decision-tree card for a fictional plant-care lesson using [TEACHER-APPROVED QUESTIONS AND OUTCOMES]. Put one root question at the top, two branch questions beneath and supplied outcomes at the bottom. Use labeled "Yes" and "No" branches, consistent rounded boxes and ample whitespace. Preserve all conditions and stopping points; do not invent watering amounts, diagnoses or species advice. Render only approved text and title. Variables: exact tree, plant context and title; teacher review is required. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

raw.text: # Characters, portraits, and storyboards Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## ART-01 — Mira and the book return ```text Create a 16:9 four-panel story sheet about Mira, an original adult mobile librarian with short black curls, round glasses, a rust cardigan and a blue bicycle basket. In left-to-right panels she finds a book on a bench, checks its plain cover, places it in her basket, then delivers it to a small library doorway. Use warm gouache illustration and soft morning light. Keep her face, outfit, bicycle and yellow book identical throughout. Exactly four equal panels; no captions, speech bubbles or legible book titles. This is a still storyboard, not video. ``` ## ART-02 — Natural portrait edit ```text Use an authorized adult portrait as the identity reference. Create a 3:4 professional portrait at eye level, changing only the background to a softly lit pale-blue studio and the clothing to a plain charcoal jacket. Preserve age, facial proportions, hairstyle, skin texture and expression. Match the new background light to the face and keep shoulders anatomically natural. Add no text, jewelry, beauty retouching or altered body shape. Variables: background color and approved wardrobe; do not use an unauthorized person's likeness. ``` ## ART-03 — Fictional station keeper ```text Create a square portrait of an original adult station keeper in a small coastal railway office. The character has silver cropped hair, a weathered navy jacket and an attentive expression; a blurred wall clock sits behind them. Use natural film-like photography, overcast window light and visible skin texture. Keep the face central with space around the head. No resemblance to a named person, official uniform insignia, readable tickets or identity documents. Variables: age range, palette and fictional occupation. ``` ## ART-04 — Seasonal courier sheet ```text Create a 16:9 four-panel character sheet of one original adult parcel courier with a long braid, green satchel and red bicycle. Show spring drizzle, summer shade, autumn wind and winter frost in equal panels. Change only seasonal outerwear and weather; lock facial features, body proportions and bicycle geometry. Use clear editorial illustration, matching camera height and neutral poses. Render only "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", and "Winter" beneath their panels. No brand logos or invented safety certifications. Variables: character design and seasonal palette. ``` ## ART-05 — Otter picture-book spread ```text Create a 2:1 picture-book spread showing a small otter helping a turtle retrieve a paper boat from reeds. Place the otter on the left and turtle on the right, with the boat near the lower center but away from the binding gutter. Use watercolor washes, warm afternoon light and readable expressions. Leave the upper-left sky blank for later typesetting. No generated words, dangerous water scene or extra characters. Keep animal scale and boat shape consistent. Variables: setting, palette and approved character references. ``` ## ART-06 — Wordless umbrella comic ```text Create a portrait 2:3 comic with six equal panels in two columns and three rows. An original adult opens a tiny umbrella, notices a wet dog, shares it, both get splashed by a puddle, discover a broad shop awning, then sit dry beneath it. Use clear ink-and-wash illustration with consistent clothing and one brown dog. Keep reading order left-to-right, top-to-bottom and actions causally connected. No dialogue, signs, extra panels or injury. Variables: character appearance and umbrella color. ``` ## ART-07 — Tea advertisement storyboard ```text Create a 16:9 six-panel still storyboard for a fictional twenty-second tea advertisement. Panels show a closed tea tin, hand opening it, leaves entering a cup, hot water pouring, steam near a window, and the cup beside the tin. Use one cream tin, one blue cup and consistent morning light. Render only the final-panel words "A quieter moment". Keep each panel a distinct shot and all props stable. No health benefits, brew temperatures or brand claims. Variables: prop design and approved final line; this is a concept, not generated footage. ``` ## ART-08 — Historical street reconstruction ```text Using [DATED EVIDENCE PACK], create a 16:9 illustration of ordinary activity at [PLACE] in [YEAR]. Preserve documented street alignment, building materials and clothing; show uncertain background areas with subdued detail. Include a narrow legend distinguishing "Documented" and "Interpretive" elements using supplied mappings. No invented inscriptions, famous faces, monuments or modern objects. Use restrained documentary illustration rather than presenting the scene as a genuine photograph. Variables: place, year, evidence and uncertainty map; obtain historical review. ``` ## ART-09 — Expression reference sheet ```text Create a 3:2 sheet of six head-and-shoulder views of one original adult character using [APPROVED CHARACTER REFERENCE]. Show neutral, curious, relieved, puzzled, determined and amused expressions in a two-by-three grid. Preserve skull shape, hair, age, outfit and camera distance; vary only eyebrows, mouth and subtle head inclination. Use soft studio illustration and a uniform pale background. Label each expression exactly once. No caricatured anatomy, identity drift or additional accessories. Variables: reference, palette and translated labels. ``` ## ART-10 — Object continuity storyboard ```text Create a 16:9 four-panel storyboard in which a red ceramic bowl moves from a shelf to a table, receives three oranges, then is carried to a window. Use the same bowl with one visible chip on its rim in every panel. Keep exactly three oranges after they appear, consistent room geometry and warm side light. Use clear realistic illustration, medium-to-close shot progression and no text. Do not move the chip, duplicate fruit or change the bowl's shape. Variables: object reference and approved room layout. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

raw.text: # Interfaces, controlled edits, and localization Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## DIG-01 — Tool library mobile interface ```text Create a 16:9 board showing three mobile screens for fictional app "Borrow Bench": catalog, item detail and reservation confirmation. Use ivory backgrounds, navy type, teal action buttons and consistent rounded cards. Show a yellow drill as the selected item. Render only "Borrow Bench", "Find a tool", "Cordless drill", "Reserve", "Collection time", "Saturday 10:00", "Reservation saved", and "View booking" in their appropriate screens. No prices, personal information or extra navigation labels. This is a static interface concept; do not imply functioning controls. ``` ## DIG-02 — CSV import review screen ```text Create a 16:9 desktop interface mockup for fictional inventory app "Stockroom". Show an import review table with columns "Item", "Quantity", and "Status"; include three supplied sample rows, one visibly marked "Needs review". Above the table render "Review your import"; below it place "Back" and "Import valid rows" buttons. Use a clean white layout with amber error emphasis and a readable sidebar containing only "Inventory". Preserve supplied data and do not display personal information. Variables: sample rows and approved copy. ``` ## DIG-03 — Regional rail homepage ```text Create a 16:9 desktop homepage concept for fictional travel planner "Local Lines". Use a large coastal-train photograph on the right and a practical search panel on the left. Render exactly "Take the slower route", "From", "To", "Travel date", and "Find journeys"; keep fields empty. Use cream background, dark-green controls and generous spacing. Add no real schedules, fares, operator logos or availability claims. Keep the train physically plausible and interface text separate from the photograph. Variables: region imagery and approved headline. ``` ## DIG-04 — Cooperative game HUD ```text Create a 16:9 static HUD concept for a fictional mountain-delivery game. Keep the central sixty percent of a snowy trail unobstructed. Place a compact compass at the top, two teammate status bars at the upper left and three inventory slots at the lower right. Render only "North", "Team", "Parcel", "Rope", and "Map". Use high-contrast shapes with restrained amber highlights, not cinematic floating holograms. Avoid real military insignia, unreadable microtext and excessive overlays. Variables: game setting and approved labels. ``` ## DIG-05 — Poster text replacement ```text Use Image 1 as the edit target and [APPROVED SOURCE-TO-TARGET TEXT MAP] as the only replacement copy. Replace the specified poster words without changing photography, illustrations, palette, margins, logos or non-target text. Preserve type weight and hierarchy; adjust line breaks only where the target language requires it. Keep punctuation, accents and reading direction correct. Remove the old words rather than duplicating them. Do not translate unspecified text or add explanations. Variables: source image and complete text map. ``` ## DIG-06 — Photo damage repair ```text Use one authorized scanned photograph as the edit target. Repair only visible dust, scratches and fold damage, reconstructing small missing areas from neighboring texture. Preserve identity, age, expression, crop, clothing, original grain and tonal range. Do not colorize a monochrome source, smooth skin, open eyes or invent background objects. Keep uncertain large missing regions unchanged rather than hallucinating details. Output one restored image without comparison labels or watermark. Variables: source photograph and explicitly marked repair areas. ``` ## DIG-07 — Three-reference product composite ```text Use Image 1 as the base tabletop scene, Image 2 as the exact ceramic cup reference and Image 3 only as the glaze-color reference. Place one cup from Image 2 on the empty coaster in Image 1 and apply only the supplied glaze hue. Preserve the base camera, crop, surrounding objects and cup geometry. Match light direction, contact shadow, perspective and reflections. Do not copy objects or text from Image 3. Add no text. Variables: three authorized images and intended cup placement. ``` ## DIG-08 — Sketch to reading room ```text Use an approved room sketch as the layout reference. Create a 4:3 realistic reading-room concept with pale oak shelves, a moss-green bench and diffuse ceiling light. Preserve every wall, window, doorway and furniture footprint from the sketch; use the material palette only to finish existing surfaces. Keep perspective coherent and aisle widths visually unchanged. Add no people, extra furniture, plants or signs. This is an illustrative concept, not a measured construction drawing. Variables: sketch and approved materials. ``` ## DIG-09 — Accessible empty state ```text Create a 3:4 mobile interface mockup for an empty saved-reading list. Use a cream background, navy text and one small illustration of three closed books. Render exactly "Nothing saved yet", "Keep useful reads in one place", and "Explore articles". Place the explanation beneath the heading and a large button below; leave comfortable margins. Use high contrast and no tiny text, loading skeleton, fake article cards or notification badges. This is a static design proposal; accessibility still requires implementation testing. ``` ## DIG-10 — Language direction comparison ```text Create a 16:9 side-by-side interface typography board from [APPROVED ENGLISH AND ARABIC COPY]. The left panel uses left-to-right alignment; the right uses natural right-to-left alignment. Preserve the same component hierarchy, spacing and two button roles while adapting reading order. Keep product photographs unchanged rather than mirroring them. Render only supplied strings, with connected Arabic glyphs and intact Latin brand names. No transliteration, duplicate source text or invented copy. Variables: paired strings and component labels; require fluent Arabic review. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

Keep explicitly multilingual strings intact; ordinary localized editions already contain translated copy. 4. Review text, counts, object geometry and layout at full size and at the intended display size. Revise one problem at a time. For data, science, history, safety or medical communication, supply reviewed evidence and obtain qualified review. Repository language coverage is not a claim that the model supports exactly those fifteen languages. The recipes describe visual intent. Actual input modes, reference limits, sizes and availability depend on the service and model variant you select. Do not treat a requested aspect ratio or a transparent-looking background as proof of API support. ## Use bestimage.ai The bestimage.ai team maintains this collection alongside its image and video generation platform. - [Qwen Image 3.0 Pro API and model entry](https://bestimage.ai/models/alibaba/qwen-image-3-0-pro/): explore the Qwen workflow relevant to this library and check the available variant before using a prompt. - [GPT Image 2 API and model entry](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/): a separate OpenAI image-generation and editing workflow for related visual tasks. raw.text: # Avatars, teams, and everyday portraits Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## AVA-01 — Workshop founder portrait ```text Use an authorized adult portrait to create a 3:4 founder image for a small furniture workshop. Preserve the person's age, facial proportions and natural skin texture. Seat them beside an unfinished wooden stool, hands resting naturally, with softly blurred tools behind. Use eye-level documentary photography and broad window light. No luxury-office props, invented awards, extra people or text. Keep clothing consistent with the supplied reference unless a replacement is explicitly provided. Variables: portrait, approved outfit and workshop setting. ``` ## AVA-02 — Circular creator avatar ```text Create a square avatar from one authorized adult portrait. Keep the face and upper shoulders within the central seventy percent so a circular crop does not cut hair or chin. Use a warm gray background, soft frontal light and a natural expression. Preserve identity, age, hairstyle and visible facial differences; remove only background clutter. No text, badges, new accessories, exaggerated smoothing or body reshaping. Variables: reference portrait and background hue. Inspect the final result at small profile-icon size. ``` ## AVA-03 — Three-person team strip ```text Using three authorized adult portraits, create a 16:9 strip of three separate headshots with equal width and matching neutral backgrounds. Preserve each person's individual face and hairstyle without blending features. Align eye height, apparent camera distance and lighting direction while keeping natural differences. Use the supplied name under each matching portrait, exactly once. No invented job titles, extra people or beautification. Variables: three references and name-to-image mapping. This task requires an editing workflow accepting all three reference images. ``` ## AVA-04 — Craft interview portrait ```text Create a 3:2 editorial portrait of an original adult bookbinder repairing a clothbound book at a wooden desk. Show hands in context, a small brush and one sheet of endpaper; keep tools logically arranged. Use side window light, restrained color and a medium shot with negative space to the right. Do not imitate a named person or add readable book text, credentials or historical claims. Keep fingers plausible and glue away from the face. Variables: craft, fictional subject and approved palette. ``` ## AVA-05 — Family cooking moment ```text Use an authorized family reference to create a 16:9 domestic scene of the same people arranging vegetables at a kitchen table. Preserve identities, age differences, relationships and clothing; use natural expressions without forcing eye contact. Keep knives and hot equipment out of reach of children. Use soft afternoon light and a believable lived-in background. No additional family members, text, exaggerated body changes or disclosure of real addresses. Variables: authorized reference and approved setting; do not infer relationships absent from the brief. ``` ## AVA-06 — Adaptive sport editorial ```text Create a 3:4 editorial portrait of an original adult wheelchair tennis player resting beside an outdoor court. Show the sports chair's wheels, frame and grip realistically and keep the racket resting across the lap. Use late-afternoon light, eye-level framing and a calm, self-directed expression. Do not portray the subject as pitiable or add inspirational slogans, medals, sponsors or medical claims. Keep anatomy and equipment plausible. Variables: fictional athlete appearance, outfit and court palette. ``` ## AVA-07 — Rainy street portrait ```text Use an authorized adult reference to create a 3:4 street-style portrait beneath a transparent umbrella. Preserve facial identity, outfit and body proportions. Place the subject near a plain brick wall with wet pavement and soft reflections; use overcast daylight rather than neon lighting. Keep umbrella ribs, handle and hand grip coherent. No extra people, visible addresses, store logos, text or changes to age. Variables: portrait, approved outerwear and background material. ``` ## AVA-08 — Author press photograph ```text Create a square press-kit portrait from an authorized adult reference. Seat the person beside a stack of plain books, with shoulders turned slightly and face toward camera. Use soft side light, an uncluttered ivory wall and realistic skin texture. Preserve hairstyle, facial features and expression. Leave room around the head for alternate crops. No invented book titles, awards, signatures, text or beauty-filter effects. Variables: portrait, approved clothing and wall color. ``` ## AVA-09 — Volunteer group illustration ```text Using [APPROVED GROUP DESCRIPTION], create a 16:9 illustration of exactly five adult volunteers sorting donated books around a long table. Give each person a distinct task and preserve supplied appearance details without caricature. Use warm editorial gouache and clear hand-object interactions. Keep aisles open and stacks stable. Add no names, organization logos, donation figures or claims about beneficiaries. Variables: approved group details and setting; fictional people should not resemble identifiable individuals. ``` ## AVA-10 — Portrait lighting study ```text Create a 3:2 two-panel lighting study using one authorized adult portrait. The left uses broad window light from camera left; the right uses the same light softened through a curtain. Lock identity, camera position, expression, clothing, crop and background. Render only "Direct window" and "Diffused window" below the matching panels. Keep changes limited to shadow softness and highlight transitions. Do not reshape the face, change skin color or simulate a different age. Variables: reference and translated labels. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

raw.text: # Social posts, covers, and creator content Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## SOC-01 — Balcony growing tutorial cover ```text Create a 3:4 social cover for a beginner balcony-growing guide. Show three small terracotta pots on a narrow shelf, each with a distinct leafy herb, and a compact watering can beneath. Use bright natural photography and a warm cream background. Render "A small balcony, a fresh start", "Three pots to begin", and "1/5" with the title occupying the upper third. No yield, health or guaranteed-growth claims. Keep pots grounded and railing geometry coherent. Variables: approved herbs and title. ``` ## SOC-02 — Triptych craft announcement ```text Create one 3:1 master image intended to be split into three square social posts. Show a long worktable with clay tools on the left, a ceramic pitcher in the center and folded linen on the right. Keep each square independently balanced; place "Make", "Share", and "Meet" in separate panels. Use consistent warm lighting and quiet cream margins. No essential object or letter may cross a crop boundary. This is a visual master, not three exported files. Variables: craft objects and three approved words. ``` ## SOC-03 — Research finding card ```text Create a 16:9 professional social card using [VERIFIED FINDING, DATA AND SOURCE]. Put one precise finding at the top, a simple supporting chart in the center and the source at the bottom. Use charcoal text and one teal accent on white. Preserve units, dates, sample limitations and uncertainty. Do not turn correlation into causation or add a dramatic percentage. Keep text readable on a phone. Variables: approved finding, dataset and citation; chart correctness needs human review. ``` ## SOC-04 — Cooking comparison thumbnail ```text Create a 16:9 video thumbnail comparing three ways of cutting a pear for serving: slices, cubes and a fan. Place three identical white plates in a row on a cobalt table, with matching pear color and consistent overhead light. Render only "One pear, three cuts" above them. Keep the cuts visually distinct and portions plausible. No nutrition claims, fake ratings, knives near hands or additional text. Variables: fruit and approved headline. ``` ## SOC-05 — Desk reset short-video cover ```text Create a 9:16 cover showing a half-tidy desk: papers aligned on the left, a closed notebook and cup on the right. Use natural overhead photography, soft shadows and a restrained sand-and-blue palette. Render "Reset your desk" in the central safe area and "Start with one surface" beneath. Keep important text away from the bottom quarter and right edge for platform overlays. No timer claim, app logos or extra copy. Variables: desk items and two-line title. ``` ## SOC-06 — Two-guest live announcement ```text Use two authorized adult portraits to create a 3:4 livestream announcement. Give each guest equal visual space, matching crop scale and neutral lighting; place names directly below their corresponding portraits. Render only [EVENT TITLE], [GUEST NAMES], [DATE] and [TIME ZONE]. Use a simple navy-and-cream grid without fake live indicators or platform logos. Preserve identities and do not invent credentials or attendance figures. Variables: two references and approved event copy. ``` ## SOC-07 — Verified quotation card ```text Create a square quotation card using [EXACT VERIFIED QUOTE] and [AUTHOR ATTRIBUTION]. Set the quote in large readable serif type on warm off-white paper; place attribution below, aligned to the same left edge. Add one small abstract blue line drawing in the lower corner. Preserve punctuation and wording exactly; do not shorten, fabricate or assign a quote to a different person. No portrait, signature or endorsement badge. Variables: verified quote, attribution and palette. ``` ## SOC-08 — Nine-step craft grid ```text Create a square three-by-three grid illustrating [NINE APPROVED CRAFT STEPS]. Use the same tabletop, hands and materials throughout, with clear progression from raw material to finished object. Label panels only "1" through "9", in left-to-right, top-to-bottom order. Keep tools and object proportions stable, and do not invent a step or show unsafe tool handling. No decorative words or duplicate panels. Variables: verified steps and materials; instructional accuracy requires review. ``` ## SOC-09 — Event recap mosaic ```text Create a 3:4 editorial recap layout for a fictional community drawing day. Arrange four image panels: sketchbooks on a table, hands drawing, a wall of unsigned sketches and empty stools at closing. Use consistent daylight and a small top heading "A day of drawing". Keep faces unidentifiable and artwork original. Do not add attendance numbers, sponsor marks or testimonial quotes. Leave a calm footer strip blank. Variables: activity and exact heading. ``` ## SOC-10 — Vertical cover crop study ```text Create a 9:16 creator-cover concept with a single red paper kite centered against a pale sky. Place "Build a paper kite" in the middle third, leaving the top fifteen percent and bottom twenty-five percent free of text. Keep the kite and headline legible within a central square crop as well. Use clean illustrative texture and a gently curved string. No platform UI, extra kites, fake buttons or small captions. Variables: object color and approved title. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).

84 complete video prompts for stories, product films, animation, education and reference-controlled scenes. Curated and maintained by the [bestimage.ai](https://bestimage.ai/) team. [简体中文](README_zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README_ja-JP.md) · [Español](README_es-ES.md) · [Language coverage](i18n/README.md) [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-bestimage.ai-4C52FE)](https://bestimage.ai/) [![FLUX 3 API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FLUX_3-API-111827)](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-text-to-video/) [![GPT Image 2 API](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT_Image_2-API-111827)](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/) ## Start with a scene you can direct 1. Browse the [84-prompt index](prompts/README.md) or [use-case matrix](docs/use-case-matrix.md). 2. Choose text, one approved first frame, two approved endpoints, or a source clip. 3. Copy the complete prompt block. Adjust the named variables, preserving object counts and continuity. 4. Use the [prompting guide](docs/prompting-guide.md) to review the result before extending the scene. Use these creative specifications as starting points for your own scenes. A requested camera move, exact phrase or endpoint match is not a guaranteed output. ## Create with bestimage.ai The bestimage.ai team maintains this independent prompt library and organizes practical image-to-video preparation and API workflows. It is not an official Black Forest Labs repository. | Starting material | bestimage.ai entry | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | A written scene | [FLUX 3 Text to Video](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-text-to-video/) | Explore a new scene, dialogue or visual explanation | | One approved image | [FLUX 3 Image to Video](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-to-video/) | Animate a supplied first-frame composition | | Opening and closing images | [FLUX 3 Start/End to Video](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-start-end-to-video/) | Request a controlled transition between two frames | | An existing clip | [FLUX 3 Video Extend](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-video-extend/) | Continue the source's movement, scene state and ambience | | A storyboard or reference-frame brief | [GPT Image 2 API](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/) | Prepare or revise **still images** before a separate video step | GPT Image 2 is a separate image workflow, not a FLUX 3 video endpoint. Approve the image and its rights before supplying it as a video reference. Generating a useful frame does not verify the resulting video's quality. プロンプトライブラリ | 分類 | プロンプト数 | 主な用途 | | --- | ---: | --- | | [映画的な物語表現](prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md) | 6 | 小さな物語、画面内の位置関係、編集のタイミング | | [広告と UGC](prompts/advertising-ugc.md) | 6 | 商品を使う動作、クリエイターのコンテンツ、サービスの一場面 | | [ドキュメンタリーと自然](prompts/documentary-nature.md) | 6 | 報道・編集用途を想定した合成シーン、じっくりとした観察 | | [アニメーションとデザイン](prompts/animation-design.md) | 6 | 紙、フェルト、粘土、タイポグラフィ、独自キャラクターの動き | | [多言語音声](prompts/multilingual-audio.md) | 6 | 正確な台詞、会話の交代、独自の歌唱や発声 | | [参照素材のワークフロー](prompts/reference-workflows.md) | 6 | 開始フレームの被写体同一性、開始・終了フレーム、連続性 | | [EC と商品](prompts/ecommerce-product.md) | 6 | 部品数、包装、素材、商品の形状 | | [旅行とホスピタリティ](prompts/travel-hospitality.md) | 6 | 相手への配慮がある交流、施設の見せ方、接客 | | [スポーツとウェルネス](prompts/sports-wellness.md) | 6 | リスクの低い動き、誰もが参加できる地域の交流 | | [教育と科学](prompts/education-science.md) | 6 | 小さく検証可能な学習内容、明確な指示 | | [建築とモビリティ](prompts/architecture-mobility.md) | 6 | 目で確認できる空間、経路、物流 | | [ソーシャルと実験的表現](prompts/social-experimental.md) | 6 | 真顔のユーモア、クリエイター同士の会話、ゲームの構想、合成用素材 | | [bestimage.ai API ワークフロー](prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md) | 12 | 文書に記載された4種類の動画モード向けの制作指示を各3件 | 各項目には、用途、モード、時間配分、画面に見える動作、音声計画、維持する条件、除外事項、調整範囲を記載しています。参照素材には明確な役割を与えてください。スタイル参照画像によって、利用権限のある商品や人物の特徴が別のものに置き換わらないようにします。 ## 注目のプロンプト 表紙のシーン: [C01 — ランタンのリレー](prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c01)：小さな実物の灯りによる合図で、架空の海辺の世界を紹介します。 表紙と5枚のイラストはオリジナルの静止画コンセプトであり、FLUX 3 の動画出力ではありません。[画像プロンプトと出典](assets/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md)もご覧ください。 ### [A01 — リネンを透かす光](prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a01) ひとつのスイッチで照明を変えながら、ランプの形状を保ちます。

### [N01 — ボタンの天文台](prompts/animation-design.md#n01) 段ボールの望遠鏡とフェルトの天文学者による、手触りを感じるミニチュアの物語です。

### [X01 — 役に立つ一文](prompts/social-experimental.md#x01) 正確な台詞と5秒間の沈黙を指定し、余計な落ちは加えません。

## モデルの機能と、この統合で利用する範囲 Black Forest Labs は FLUX 3 をマルチモーダルモデルと説明しており、テキスト・画像・動画の参照素材、キーフレーム、動画の継続、ネイティブ音声を使う動画生成について文書化しています。動画、画像、アクション、オープンウェイトの各構成要素は、それぞれ公開状況が異なります。利用可否や機能を前提にする前に、[公式モデルページ](https://bfl.ai/models/flux-3)と[リリース概要](https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3)を確認してください。 モデル全体の説明だけでは、すべての提供サービスがすべての入力形式に対応しているとは判断できません。このライブラリの bestimage.ai ワークフローパックでは、文書に記載された4種類の動画モードだけを扱います。特に、開始フレーム1枚を指定する `image_url` は、汎用的な複数参照素材の配列ではありません。 ## 言語別の収録範囲 - 案内用 README は4言語：英語、簡体字中国語、日本語、スペイン語。 - 英語以外のシーンファイルは11言語：中国語、日本語、スペイン語、フランス語、ドイツ語、韓国語、ブラジルポルトガル語、イタリア語、アラビア語、ロシア語、インドネシア語。 - 各シーンファイルは、共通の原文3件、X01・E01・L01 を翻訳しています。これら33件の翻訳は、**33件の追加オリジナルプロンプトではありません**。 - 全84件のプロンプトと制作ガイドは英語で保守しています。各言語のファイルはライブラリ全体の翻訳ではありません。 具体的なファイルと翻訳範囲は[言語ディレクトリ](i18n/README.md)を参照してください。 ## 結果を公開する前に確認すること 使用許諾を得た参照画像と、本人の同意を得た容姿・声を使ってください。動き、身体の構造、物体の数、台詞、文字、開始・終了フレームの連続性を確認します。合成された商品実演は商品の性能を証明するものではなく、架空の施設のシーンは実際のサービス提供を裏付けるものではありません。業務上重要な文言と検証済みの測定値は、後編集で追加してください。 ## 貢献する 役立つプロンプト、作例、翻訳を歓迎します。[貢献ガイド](CONTRIBUTING.md)をご覧ください。 ## bestimage.ai について このプロンプト集は [bestimage.ai](https://bestimage.ai/) チームが編集・保守し、実践的な制作ワークフローを画像・動画モデルの API につなげます。 ## bestimage.ai のアフィリエイトプログラムに参加 チュートリアル、プロンプト、API 連携事例を公開していますか？[bestimage.ai アフィリエイトプログラム](https://bestimage.ai/affiliate-program/)に参加し、読者や視聴者に bestimage.ai を紹介して報酬を得られます。 - 紹介したユーザーの初回の対象有料注文に対して **20%**。 - そのユーザーの**登録後 60 日以内**の、2 回目以降の対象有料注文に対して **10%**。 対象注文と支払いの条件は[現行のアフィリエイト契約](https://bestimage.ai/affiliate-agreement/)に従います。 ## ライセンス [MIT](LICENSE).

# Awesome FLUX 3 提示词库

84条完整视频提示词，涵盖故事、产品短片、动画、教育及参考素材控制场景。由 [bestimage.ai](https://bestimage.ai/) 团队整理与维护。 [English](README.md) · 简体中文 · [日本語](README_ja-JP.md) · [Español](README_es-ES.md) · [语言覆盖范围](i18n/README.md) [![官网](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-bestimage.ai-4C52FE)](https://bestimage.ai/) [![FLUX 3 API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FLUX_3-API-111827)](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-text-to-video/) [![GPT Image 2 API](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT_Image_2-API-111827)](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/) ## 使用 bestimage.ai 创作 bestimage.ai 团队维护这个独立提示词库，整理实用的图生视频前期准备与 API 工作流。本项目不是 Black Forest Labs 官方仓库。 | 起始素材 | bestimage.ai 入口 | 用途 | | --- | --- | --- | | 文字场景描述 | [FLUX 3 文生视频](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-text-to-video/) | 探索新场景、对白或视觉讲解 | | 一张已确认的图像 | [FLUX 3 图生视频](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-to-video/) | 让提供的首帧构图动起来 | | 开场与结尾图像 | [FLUX 3 首尾帧生视频](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-start-end-to-video/) | 要求两帧之间形成受控过渡 | | 已有视频片段 | [FLUX 3 视频续写](https://bestimage.ai/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-video-extend/) | 延续源视频的动作、场景状态与环境氛围 | | 分镜或参考帧创作说明 | [GPT Image 2 API](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/) | 在独立的视频制作步骤之前，准备或修改**静态图像** | GPT Image 2 是独立的图像工作流，不是 FLUX 3 视频接口。将图像用作视频参考之前，应确认图像内容及其使用权。生成一张可用的参考帧，并不能验证后续视频的质量。 [12条面向 API 的创作说明](prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md)与文档列出的模型 ID 和媒体字段相对应。[集成指南](docs/bestimage-ai-flux-3-api.md)使用 **bestimage.ai 的 API 主机 `https://api.flaq.ai`**，请使用在 bestimage.ai 账户中获取的 API 密钥。 ## 精选提示词 封面场景: [C01 — 灯笼接力](prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c01)：一个由场景内灯光发出的微小信号，带出虚构的海岸世界。 封面和五张配图是原创静态概念图，并非 FLUX 3 视频输出。完整提示词与来源见[素材说明](assets/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md)。 ### [A01 — 穿过亚麻的光](prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a01) 用一次开关操作改变照明，同时保持灯具的几何形态。

### [N01 — 纽扣天文台](prompts/animation-design.md#n01) 以纸板望远镜和毛毡天文学家，讲述富有触感的微缩故事。

### [E01 — 两块隔板，一个位置](prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e01) 组装说明明确区分三个产品零件与作为道具的笔记本。

## 模型能力与 API 支持范围 Black Forest Labs 将 FLUX 3 描述为多模态模型，并在文档中介绍了支持文字、图像与视频参考、关键帧、续写和原生音频的视频生成能力。其视频、图像、动作及开放权重组件具有不同的开放状态。依赖某项访问权限或能力之前，请查看[官方模型页面](https://bfl.ai/models/flux-3)与[发布介绍](https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3)。 模型层面的整体介绍，并不意味着每个服务提供方都开放了全部输入方式。本提示词库的 bestimage.ai 工作流包仅使用文档列出的四种视频模式。尤其需要注意，单个 `image_url` 首帧字段并不等于通用的多参考素材数组。 ## 语言覆盖范围 - 四份项目介绍：英语、简体中文、日语和西班牙语。 - 十一个非英语场景文件：中文、日语、西班牙语、法语、德语、韩语、巴西葡萄牙语、意大利语、阿拉伯语、俄语和印度尼西亚语。 - 每个场景文件都翻译相同的三个标准场景：X01、E01 和 L01。这33条译文**不是额外的33条原创提示词**。 - 完整的84条提示词及制作指南以英语维护。本地化文件不是全库完整译文。 具体文件和覆盖范围请查看[语言目录](i18n/README.md)。 ## 发布结果前先检查 使用已获授权的参考图，以及已获本人同意使用的身份特征和声音。检查动作、人体结构、物体数量、对白、文字和首尾帧连续性。合成产品演示不能证明产品性能；虚构场所的场景也不能证明现实中确有相应服务。业务关键信息和已核实的测量数据应在后期制作中添加。 ## 参与贡献 欢迎分享实用提示词、案例和译文，请先阅读[贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。 ## 关于 bestimage.ai 本提示词库由 [bestimage.ai](https://bestimage.ai/) 团队整理与维护，将实用创作流程与图像、视频模型 API 连接起来。 ## 加入 bestimage.ai 联盟推广计划 制作教程、分享提示词或发布 API 集成案例？加入 [bestimage.ai 联盟推广计划](https://bestimage.ai/affiliate-program/)，向你的受众推荐 bestimage.ai，并获得推荐佣金。 - 受推荐用户的首笔有效付费订单，佣金为 **20%**。 - 该用户**注册后 60 天内**的后续有效付费订单，佣金为 **10%**。 订单资格与结算以[现行联盟协议](https://bestimage.ai/affiliate-agreement/)为准。 ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE).

# Concept illustrations and generation prompts

This collection includes six original concept illustrations: one cover and five scene previews, generated on 2026-08-28 with Codex's built-in image generation tool. Each image was created from the corresponding text prompt below. The bestimage.ai SVG logo is a separate brand asset.

These are **static concept illustrations, not FLUX 3 video outputs**. They show composition, materials and a moment within each scene; they do not demonstrate motion, speech or temporal consistency.

## Image inventory

| Image | Scene | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [flux-3-prompts-hero.png](flux-3-prompts-hero.png) | [C01](../prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c01) | Repository cover |
| [featured/light-through-linen.png](featured/light-through-linen.png) | [A01](../prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a01) | Product concept frame |
| [featured/button-observatory.png](featured/button-observatory.png) | [N01](../prompts/animation-design.md#n01) | Stop-motion concept frame |
| [featured/two-dividers.png](featured/two-dividers.png) | [E01](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e01) | Assembly concept frame |
| [featured/shadow-card.png](featured/shadow-card.png) | [L01](../prompts/education-science.md#l01) | Educational concept frame |
| [featured/one-useful-sentence.png](featured/one-useful-sentence.png) | [X01](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x01) | Social/dialogue concept frame |

Follow each scene link for the complete video prompt. A preview may depict a later moment in the scene; prepare a compatible first frame before using it as an image-to-video input.

## Cover — The lantern relay

```text
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: wide repository cover, one coherent cinematic scene
Primary request: a static concept frame for a quiet coastal science-fiction short about a practical lantern signal
Scene: an older lighthouse keeper in an olive knitted coat stands on a stone balcony above a dark harbor, setting one rectangular amber lantern onto the parapet; a single distant window shows a small warm light
Style: grounded cinematic production art, photorealistic materials, restrained atmosphere
Composition: wide establishing view from behind and beside the keeper at shoulder height, readable lantern and distant harbor, no montage or panel divisions
Lighting: cool evening ambience, warm lantern reflection on damp stone
Constraints: one keeper, one lantern, plausible hands and balcony, no futuristic skyline, spacecraft, weapons, readable text, logos or watermark
Output aspect ratio: 21:9.
```

## A01 — Light through linen

```text
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: vertical concept frame for a table-lamp motion brief
Primary request: one unbranded table lamp with a pleated cream linen shade and cylindrical terracotta base, standing on a simple wooden tabletop
Scene: modest quiet interior, a single black cable with one inline switch remains fully plausible and visible
Composition: three-quarter product view, complete lamp inside frame, clear space above, no hands in this frame
Lighting: warm light transmitted through the shade against soft afternoon window light
Materials: natural linen fibers, matte clay base, ordinary wood grain
Constraints: one lamp, no duplicated controls, base not glowing, no text, logos, watermarks, certifications or performance claims
Output aspect ratio: 9:16.
```

## N01 — The button observatory

```text
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: wide static stop-motion concept frame
Primary request: a tiny felt astronomer with a rust-colored cap examining one white four-hole button beside a simple cardboard telescope in a tabletop observatory
Scene: stitched blue paper dome with one opening, visible wooden crank, small paper pedestal beside the telescope
Style: tactile handcrafted miniature, visible felt seams, cardstock fibers and slight handmade imperfections
Composition: miniature-wide view with the worktable edge visible, one character and readable small mechanism
Lighting: soft practical miniature light with gentle shadows
Constraints: exactly one white button with four holes, no human hands, glossy plastic, real sky replacement, existing franchise character, text, logos or watermark
Output aspect ratio: 16:9.
```

## E01 — Two dividers, one place

```text
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: wide assembly concept frame
Primary request: a small wooden desk organizer assembled from exactly one rectangular base and two identical upright dividers, with one closed blue notebook standing between them
Scene: plain workbench, soft daylight from the left
Composition: clear near-overhead three-quarter angle showing the two parallel slots, both dividers and the notebook as a separate prop
Style: honest product photography, natural wood grain, no showroom embellishment
Constraints: three wooden product parts total, one notebook, no hands in this final frame, extra dividers, fasteners, pens, text, logos, watermarks or load claims
Output aspect ratio: 16:9.
```

### E01 image edit

The notebook was repositioned between the two dividers using the initial generated image as the edit reference.

```text
Change only the position of the single closed blue notebook: move it into the central gap BETWEEN the two existing wooden upright dividers. The notebook must stand on the base inside that gap, with the nearer divider in front of the notebook and the farther divider behind it. Keep both wooden dividers, the rectangular base, their geometry, the camera angle, natural wood, workbench, daylight and all other details unchanged. Exactly three wooden product parts total: one base and two identical dividers. One notebook only, no extra dividers or props, no text or logos. Output aspect ratio: 16:9.
```

## L01 — Move the card, not the light

```text
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: wide static classroom concept frame
Primary request: a clear small tabletop shadow demonstration, one lamp on the left shining toward a vertical white screen on the right with one opaque square card between them
Scene: a single adult hand grips a short handle supporting the card near the lamp; the screen shows one enlarged square shadow
Composition: fixed side three-quarter view showing lamp, card, screen and cast shadow together without obscuring the light path
Style: clean, physically plausible educational photography
Constraints: one lamp, one card, one screen, single consistent enlarged shadow, constant light, no arrows, labels, text, logos or watermark
Output aspect ratio: 16:9.
```

## X01 — One useful sentence

```text
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: vertical concept frame for a deadpan social short
Primary request: one adult facilitator in a gray jumper sitting sincerely at a plain meeting table, looking toward the camera during an awkwardly quiet pause
Scene: small tabletop microphone and one closed notebook are the only table objects, ordinary office background and lighting
Composition: locked phone-camera medium framing, natural hands resting on the table, unexaggerated expression
Style: candid workplace photography with real skin texture, no glamour retouching
Constraints: exactly one person, microphone and notebook, no readable screen, visible company branding, captions, logos, watermark or extra props
Output aspect ratio: 9:16.
```

## Review after generation

Check scene-to-image agreement, object counts, hands, materials, logo absence and educational shadow geometry. Record the real tool/model and any edits. Use original illustrations and preserve applicable source credits.

# FLUX 3 prompting guide: from idea to usable shot

Maintained by the bestimage.ai team. FLUX 3 prompts work best as compact directing briefs. This guide turns a vague idea into a testable prompt without pretending that prompt text alone replaces production judgment.

The [84-scene index](../prompts/README.md) contains creative specifications, not model-tested results.

## 1. Choose the generation mode before writing

| You already have | Use this strategy | Lock first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Only an idea or script | Text-to-video | world, subject description, timeline |
| A product, person, illustration, or first frame | Image-to-video | identity, geometry, composition, light |
| Several images with different jobs | Multi-reference | one role per image; reject cross-contamination |
| Required visual milestones | Ordered keyframes | exact order, target times, invariant geometry |
| A clip whose action should continue | Video continuation | final frame, momentum, camera, exposure, audio bed |
| A clip whose style or context should change | Video-to-video | source elements to preserve vs transform |

The table describes creative input strategies, not interchangeable API parameters. bestimage.ai's documented FLUX 3 modes expose text, one first-frame image, start/end images, and video extension. Its single `image_url` field does not establish support for arbitrary identity/style/reference arrays. Multi-reference and ordered multi-keyframe strategies above require an interface that explicitly supports them. For this edition's bestimage.ai recipes, prepare one approved composite first frame or a matched pair of endpoints; never invent extra request fields.

Do not ask every reference to control everything. A useful role statement looks like this:

```text
Image 1 controls identity and wardrobe only.
Image 2 controls environment, time of day, and palette only.
Clip 1 controls camera path and movement timing only.
Do not import people, text, logos, or props from style and motion references.
```

## 2. Define the end frame early

The last three to five seconds determine whether a clip is editable. Decide whether the ending should:

- hold a product hero angle;
- settle on a readable title;
- provide negative space for post-production copy;
- match the start frame for a loop;
- preserve motion for continuation;
- stop in silence for an editorial cut.

If the final frame matters, describe camera deceleration, subject behavior, prop state, and hold duration. “End cinematically” is not actionable.

## 3. Write a readable timeline

Each time range should contain one main action and one camera intention. A practical 20-second structure is:

```text
00:00-00:05 — Establish the world and subject.
00:05-00:12 — Perform the primary action with visible cause and effect.
00:12-00:16 — Introduce a turn, response, or proof point.
00:16-00:20 — Decelerate into a deliberate final frame.
```

Avoid packing dialogue, camera orbit, costume change, object transformation, weather change, and title animation into the same four seconds.

## 4. Separate camera, subject, and environment motion

Write these as three independent layers:

```text
Camera: track backward at walking speed, chest height, never cross the action axis.
Subject: walk forward, open the umbrella once, then keep it open.
Environment: rain falls at a constant angle; trees and coat respond to the same crosswind.
```

This makes failures easier to diagnose. If a result feels unstable, remove one motion layer before adding adjectives.

## 5. Lock identity and product geometry

List only details that are visible and important:

- facial structure, age, hair, distinctive mark;
- body proportions and handedness;
- wardrobe layers, color, fasteners, accessories;
- product silhouette, part count, label area, fill level, material;
- object scale relative to hands and environment.

Repeat the lock after any major style change. Avoid vague instructions such as “keep everything the same.”

## 6. Prompt physical causality

Strong video feels causal: force precedes motion, sound follows impact, weight affects acceleration, and wetness accumulates instead of resetting.

Check:

- hands touch an object before it moves;
- wheels rotate at the distance traveled;
- liquid level, spill, and reflection remain consistent;
- cloth, hair, dust, and plants respond to the same wind;
- shadows and reflections share one light source;
- props stay where they were placed;
- the camera cannot pass through walls or people.

## 7. Design audio as four layers

```text
Dialogue: exact quoted words, language, voice character, pace, pauses.
Ambience: the continuous acoustic space.
Foley: visible causes—footsteps, fabric, tools, doors, water.
Music: instrument, tempo, entry, exit, and intensity; or explicitly none.
```

For multilingual speech, state what must not happen:

```text
Speak the quoted Japanese line exactly once.
Do not translate, paraphrase, repeat, subtitle, or add words.
Natural conversational delivery; no announcer cadence.
```

## 8. Decide whether text belongs in generation

Generate text when it is visually central and short: a title, label, chapter card, or sign that interacts with the scene. Add text in post when it is legally sensitive, frequently updated, data-heavy, price-based, or needs exact brand typography.

When generating text:

```text
Render exactly once: "SEE IT. SOLVE IT."
Warm-white geometric sans serif, centered, stable for three seconds.
No extra words, translation, punctuation, logo, or decorative glyphs.
```

## 9. Build a useful avoid list

An avoid list should target likely failures, not repeat generic quality language.

Useful:

```text
Avoid: duplicate bottle, changing liquid level, cap drift, invented label,
warped reflection, extra copy, logo, watermark.
```

Less useful:

```text
Avoid: bad quality, ugly, mistakes, low resolution.
```

## 10. Iterate with one controlled change

Use a simple record:

| Version | Changed | Kept fixed | Result | Next decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | baseline | — | identity good; camera too fast | slow camera only |
| v2 | camera speed | identity, action, audio | stable; end frame short | add 3-second hold |
| v3 | end hold | everything else | usable | render final |

Do not rewrite the whole prompt after every result. One-change iteration preserves what already works.

## 11. Production review checklist

- The concept is original or properly licensed.
- Every reference has a declared role and usage rights.
- Identity, voice, logo, and location permissions are documented.
- Visible claims are supportable; medical, financial, and performance claims are reviewed.
- Dialogue, captions, and typography match the intended locale.
- Physics, continuity, hands, text, and reflections are reviewed frame by frame.
- Generated content is not presented as documentary evidence or an official benchmark.
- A human approves the final edit, audio mix, and release context.

## 12. Access and parameters

FLUX 3 capabilities, endpoints, duration, resolution bands, pricing, and available input modes may change during rollout. Use the [official FLUX 3 model page](https://bfl.ai/models/flux-3) and [official overview](https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3) as the source of truth rather than copying old API examples into production.

## 13. Prepare still references with GPT Image 2

The [bestimage.ai GPT Image 2 API page](https://bestimage.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2/) is a separate image workflow. Use it to explore storyboard compositions or revise an authorized still, then inspect identity, product geometry, object count and rights before using that image in a FLUX 3 video request. A generated image is not proof of a real product, venue, event or a successful video workflow.

For two endpoints, prepare compatible camera position, perspective, object inventory and lighting. If the desired action cannot plausibly connect them, revise the brief before spending on video generation.

## 14. Match request constraints without changing the brief silently

Use a supported ratio and duration when authoring the scene; these recipes use the documented 5–20 second range and selected supported ratios. Inspect current limits at submission time. A creative cadence such as stop motion is not an `fps` parameter. A requested endpoint match is not a promise of exact pixels.

Copy the full prompt, measure its length and preserve all role, dialogue and continuity instructions. If a provider limit prevents submission, revise deliberately; do not truncate the prompt automatically. Keep model IDs and source URLs outside the natural-language prompt.

# FLUX 3 use-case matrix

Choose by production goal and actual starting material. These are creative specifications, not tested demonstrations of the named use cases. Follow the [prompting guide](prompting-guide.md) and inspect one short result before adding complexity.

| Need | Starting material | Recipes | First review |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Quiet narrative | Text | [C01](../prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c01), [C05](../prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c05), [F01](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#f01) | Visible cause before reaction |
| Parallel or edited narrative | Text | [C02](../prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c02), [C06](../prompts/cinematic-storytelling.md#c06) | Screen geography and cut timing |
| Homeware campaign | Approved first frame | [A01](../prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a01), [E05](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e05) | Exact geometry, no invented performance |
| Credible creator gesture | Text | [A02](../prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a02), [X01](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x01) | Count, dialogue and natural pauses |
| Product assembly or handling | Text or first frame as specified | [E01](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e01), [A04](../prompts/advertising-ugc.md#a04), [F04](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#f04) | Contact, part count and no hidden step |
| Packaging workflow | Text or first frame as specified | [E03](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e03), [E04](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e04) | One dose/order, no health or dispatch claim |
| Nature-style observation | Text | [D02](../prompts/documentary-nature.md#d02), [D05](../prompts/documentary-nature.md#d05) | Anatomy, scale and disclosure |
| Handcrafted animation | Text | [N01](../prompts/animation-design.md#n01), [N05](../prompts/animation-design.md#n05) | Material and intentional stylization |
| Generated typography test | Text | [N04](../prompts/animation-design.md#n04) | Exact glyphs; manually review every line |
| Bilingual dialogue | Text | [M02](../prompts/multilingual-audio.md#m02), [F02](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#f02) | Assigned voices, no translation or overlap |
| Original vocal excerpt | Text | [M03](../prompts/multilingual-audio.md#m03) | Original melody, lyric accuracy, breath |
| Portrait motion | Consented first frame | [R01](../prompts/reference-workflows.md#r01), [M05](../prompts/multilingual-audio.md#m05) | Identity and subtle motion |
| Prepared composite animation | One approved combined still | [R04](../prompts/reference-workflows.md#r04) | No cross-reference contamination |
| Endpoint match | Two approved frames | [R02](../prompts/reference-workflows.md#r02), [R05](../prompts/reference-workflows.md#r05), [F07](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#f07) | Constant geometry and practical path |
| Clip continuation | Authorized clip | [R03](../prompts/reference-workflows.md#r03), [F10–F12](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#video-extend) | No initial frame or sound reset |
| Property or access detail | Actual licensed first frame | [T01](../prompts/travel-hospitality.md#t01), [T03](../prompts/travel-hospitality.md#t03), [B01](../prompts/architecture-mobility.md#b01) | No changed architecture or invented dimensions |
| Respectful travel interaction | Text | [T02](../prompts/travel-hospitality.md#t02), [T04](../prompts/travel-hospitality.md#t04) | Consent and no unverified route advice |
| Inclusive community scene | Text | [S04](../prompts/sports-wellness.md#s04) | Agency, room clearance and no medical claim |
| Simple sports motion | Text | [S03](../prompts/sports-wellness.md#s03) | One complete ball path and contact |
| Classroom cause and effect | Text | [L01](../prompts/education-science.md#l01), [L02](../prompts/education-science.md#l02), [F03](../prompts/bestimage-api-workflows.md#f03) | Scientific sequence, clear limitations |
| Listening lesson | Text | [L03](../prompts/education-science.md#l03) | Word-to-card mapping and intelligible speech |
| Small logistics scene | Text | [B03](../prompts/architecture-mobility.md#b03), [B04](../prompts/architecture-mobility.md#b04) | Object state and handoff order |
| Original game world | Text | [X03](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x03) | Original design and understandable mechanic |
| Compositing plate | Approved first frame | [X04](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x04) | Uncropped hands, clean edges and hold |
| Designed loop | Matching endpoints | [X05](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x05) | Return every object, no hidden dissolve |

## Format choices

- Vertical delivery: 9:16; 3:4 is also used in selected design and illustration briefs.
- Product detail: 1:1.
- General editorial and education: 16:9.
- Wider narrative: 2:1 or 21:9.
- Existing footage: preserve its supported source ratio.

These are creative choices. Confirm the actual provider's allowed values before submitting. Do not silently substitute an unsupported crop or duration.

## Reduce the first test

For unstable identity, start with a blink and a fixed camera. For hand failures, use one object and one contact. For typography, first test a stationary short phrase. For audio, begin with one voice and one short sentence. For continuation, compare the source's last frame and sound with the new clip's first frame and sound.

# نصوص توجيهية لـ FLUX 3 بالعربية (`ar`)

ترجمات لثلاثة مشاهد مشتركة، يتولى فريق bestimage.ai صيانتها. هذه مجموعة مختارة وليست ترجمة كاملة للنصوص التوجيهية الـ84 في المكتبة. المشاهد مقترحات إبداعية. تتطابق المعرّفات والتوقيت وحركات الكاميرا وقيود الاستمرارية مع النصوص الإنجليزية النهائية.

[الصفحة الرئيسية](../README.md) · [فهرس اللغات](README.md) · [المصادر ونسب الأعمال](../docs/sources.md)

## I18N-01 — جملة واحدة مفيدة

**الاستخدام:** مقطع قصير للشبكات الاجتماعية بكوميديا تُؤدّى بجدية · **الوضع:** تحويل النص إلى فيديو  
**التنسيق:** 9:16، مدة 15 ثانية · **القابل للتعديل:** الملابس، دون تغيير الوقفة أو الحوار.  
**الأصل الإنجليزي:** [X01](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x01).

```text
شخص بالغ يدير الجلسة، يرتدي كنزة رمادية، يجلس إلى طاولة اجتماعات بسيطة. لا توجد عليها أدوات سوى ميكروفون مكتبي صغير ودفتر مغلق. لقطة متوسطة ثابتة بكاميرا هاتف؛ إضاءة مكتبية عادية.
00:00–00:05 — يشغّل مدير الجلسة الميكروفون بزرّه الموجود، وينظر نحو الكاميرا ويقول بهدوء وبعربية فصحى طبيعية، حرفيًا: «لدينا وقت لجملة واحدة مفيدة.»
00:05–00:10 — حافظ على خمس ثوانٍ كاملة من الصمت الجاد. ينظر مدير الجلسة مرة واحدة إلى الدفتر المغلق دون فتحه.
00:10–00:15 — يرفع نظره مجددًا ويقول حرفيًا: «كان هذا كل شيء.» يطفئ الميكروفون ويبقى جالسًا.
الصوت: تهوية هادئة، نقرتان خفيفتان للزر، وكلام طبيعي. بلا موسيقى أو ضحك أو رد فعل من جمهور.
النص: لا شيء؛ بلا ترجمة نصية تلقائية.
ثبّت: شخص واحد وميكروفون واحد ودفتر واحد؛ الوجه واليدان والملابس والتأطير نفسها.
تجنّب: حوارًا إضافيًا، تمثيلًا مبالغًا فيه، فتح الدفتر، حضور أشخاص جدد، هوية بصرية لشركة وهمية، أو علامة مائية.
```

## I18N-02 — فاصلان ومكان واحد

**الاستخدام:** تصور لتجميع منظّم مكتبي دون أدوات · **الوضع:** تحويل النص إلى فيديو  
**التنسيق:** 16:9، مدة 20 ثانية · **القابل للتعديل:** درجة لون الخشب، دون تغيير عدد القطع.  
**الأصل الإنجليزي:** [E01](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e01).

```text
أظهر منظّمًا مكتبيًا خشبيًا صغيرًا على منضدة عمل بسيطة. يتكوّن المنتج من ثلاث قطع بالضبط: قاعدة مستطيلة فيها شقّان متوازيان وفاصلان رأسيان متماثلان. يدا شخص بالغ بلا حُليّ. كاميرا علوية ثابتة وضوء نهار ناعم من اليسار.
00:00–00:05 — أظهر القطع الثلاث منفصلة. تلتقط اليد اليمنى أحد الفاصلين، وتثبّت اليسرى القاعدة.
00:05–00:11 — أدخل ذلك الفاصل في الشق الأول بحركة انزلاق حتى يستقر بالكامل في موضعه دون بروز عند نقطة التثبيت. أدخل الفاصل الثاني في الشق الثاني. بلا قطع خفي بين اللقطات وبلا أدوات تثبيت إضافية.
00:11–00:16 — ضع دفترًا أزرق مغلقًا واحدًا في وضع رأسي بين الفاصلين. الدفتر من أدوات المشهد، وليس قطعة إضافية من المنظّم.
00:16–00:20 — اسحب اليدين وأبقِ الترتيب المكتمل ظاهرًا. يظل الدفتر مسنودًا دون تغيّر حجمه.
الصوت: صوتا تلامس خفيفان للخشب، وصوت ورق على خشب، وأجواء غرفة هادئة. بلا حوار أو موسيقى.
النص: لا شيء.
ثبّت: القطع الثلاث والشقّان وعروق الخشب والدفتر نفسها طوال المشهد.
تجنّب: التجميع الذاتي، فواصل إضافية، اختفاء الأصابع، براغي جديدة، ادعاءات مختلقة عن قدرة التحمل، نصًا، شعارات، أو علامة مائية.
```

## I18N-03 — حرّك البطاقة لا الضوء

**الاستخدام:** عرض تمهيدي لشرح الظلال · **الوضع:** تحويل النص إلى فيديو  
**التنسيق:** 16:9، مدة 15 ثانية · **القابل للتعديل:** شكل البطاقة، مع إبقاء الضوء والشاشة ثابتين.  
**الأصل الإنجليزي:** [L01](../prompts/education-science.md#l01).

```text
أنشئ عرضًا توضيحيًا بسيطًا في غرفة صف. يضيء مصباح صغير على اليسار باتجاه شاشة بيضاء رأسية على اليمين. تقف بينهما بطاقة مربعة معتمة واحدة مثبّتة على مقبض قصير. تُظهر كاميرا جانبية ثابتة المصباح والبطاقة والظل معًا.
00:00–00:05 — حافظ على الترتيب الأولي. تمسك يد شخص بالغ بمقبض البطاقة دون حجب المصباح.
00:05–00:10 — قرّب البطاقة ببطء من المصباح، على امتداد الخط الواصل بين المصباح والشاشة. يكبر ظلها على الشاشة. لا يتحرك المصباح ولا الشاشة.
00:10–00:15 — أوقف الحركة وحافظ على الترتيب الجديد. تُبقي اليد البطاقة ثابتة.
التعليق الصوتي: قل بعربية فصحى واضحة، حرفيًا: «يبقى الضوء هنا. تقريب البطاقة من الضوء يجعل ظلها أكبر.»
الصوت: أجواء صف هادئة خلف التعليق الصوتي؛ بلا موسيقى.
النص: لا شيء.
ثبّت: مصباح واحد وبطاقة واحدة وشاشة واحدة، وسطوع ثابت وظل واحد متّسق.
تجنّب: تقلّص الظل أثناء الحركة، مصادر ضوء متعددة، بطاقة طافية، تغيّر الشاشة، تسميات إضافية، شعارات، أو علامة مائية.
```

# FLUX-3-Prompts auf Deutsch (`de-DE`)

Drei Übersetzungen gemeinsamer Szenen, gepflegt vom bestimage.ai-Team. Diese Auswahl ist keine vollständige Übersetzung der 84 Prompts der Sammlung. Die Szenen sind kreative Entwürfe. Kennungen, Zeitabläufe, Gegenstände und Vorgaben bleiben über alle Sprachen hinweg gleich.

[Projektübersicht auf Englisch](../README.md) · [Sprachübersicht](README.md) · [Quellen und Urheberangaben](../docs/sources.md)

## I18N-01 — Ein hilfreicher Satz

[Englische Ausgangsszene: X01](../prompts/social-experimental.md#x01)

**Einsatz:** kurzer Beitrag für soziale Medien mit trockenem Humor · **Modus:** Text zu Video  
**Format:** 9:16, 15 Sekunden · **Anpassbar:** Kleidung, nicht die Pause oder der Dialog.

```text
Eine erwachsene Person, die eine Besprechung moderiert, sitzt in einem grauen Pullover an einem schlichten Besprechungstisch. Ein kleines Tischmikrofon und ein geschlossenes Notizbuch sind die einzigen Gegenstände. Feste halbnahe Einstellung mit einer Handykamera; gewöhnliche Bürobeleuchtung.
00:00–00:05 — Die Person schaltet das Mikrofon mit dessen vorhandenem Knopf ein, blickt zur Kamera und sagt ruhig auf Deutsch, genau: „Wir haben Zeit für einen hilfreichen Satz.“
00:05–00:10 — Fünf volle Sekunden ernst gemeinte Stille halten. Die Person blickt einmal auf das geschlossene Notizbuch, öffnet es aber nicht.
00:10–00:15 — Wieder aufblicken und genau sagen: „Das war er.“ Das Mikrofon ausschalten und sitzen bleiben.
TON: Leise Lüftung, zwei leise Knopfklicks und natürliche Sprache. Keine Musik, kein Lachen und keine Publikumsreaktion.
TEXT: Keiner; keine automatischen Untertitel.
BEIBEHALTEN: Eine Person, ein Mikrofon, ein Notizbuch; unverändertes Gesicht, Hände, Kleidung und Bildausschnitt.
VERMEIDEN: zusätzlichen Dialog, übertriebenes Schauspiel, Öffnen des Notizbuchs, neue Teilnehmende, erfundene Unternehmenskennzeichen oder Wasserzeichen.
```

## I18N-02 — Zwei Trennwände, ein Platz

[Englische Ausgangsszene: E01](../prompts/ecommerce-product.md#e01)

**Einsatz:** Konzept für den werkzeuglosen Aufbau eines Schreibtisch-Organizers · **Modus:** Text zu Video  
**Format:** 16:9, 20 Sekunden · **Anpassbar:** Holzfarbton, nicht die Anzahl der Teile.

```text
Einen kleinen Schreibtisch-Organizer aus Holz auf einer schlichten Werkbank zeigen. Das Produkt besteht aus genau drei Teilen: einer rechteckigen Grundplatte mit zwei parallelen Nuten und zwei identischen aufrechten Trennwänden. Die Hände einer erwachsenen Person tragen keinen Schmuck. Feste Kamera in Draufsicht, weiches Tageslicht von links.
00:00–00:05 — Alle drei Teile getrennt zeigen. Die rechte Hand nimmt eine Trennwand auf; die linke hält die Grundplatte fest.
00:05–00:11 — Diese Trennwand in die erste Nut schieben, bis sie bündig sitzt. Die zweite Trennwand in die zweite Nut einsetzen. Kein versteckter Schnitt und keine zusätzlichen Befestigungsteile.
00:11–00:16 — Ein geschlossenes blaues Notizbuch aufrecht zwischen die Trennwände stellen. Das Notizbuch ist eine Requisite und kein zusätzliches Bauteil des Organizers.
00:16–00:20 — Beide Hände zurückziehen und die fertige Anordnung im Bild halten. Das Notizbuch bleibt abgestützt, ohne seine Größe zu verändern.
TON: Zwei sanfte Holzberührungen, Papier auf Holz und leise Raumgeräusche. Kein Dialog und keine Musik.
TEXT: Keiner.
BEIBEHALTEN: Durchgehend dieselben drei Teile, zwei Nuten, dieselbe Holzmaserung und dasselbe Notizbuch.
VERMEIDEN: Selbstmontage, zusätzliche Trennwände, verschwindende Finger, neue Schrauben, erfundene Angaben zur Tragfähigkeit, Text, Logos oder Wasserzeichen.
```

## I18N-03 — Die Karte bewegen, nicht das Licht

[Englische Ausgangsszene: L01](../prompts/education-science.md#l01)

**Einsatz:** einfache Demonstration zur Schattenbildung · **Modus:** Text zu Video  
**Format:** 16:9, 15 Sekunden · **Anpassbar:** Kartenform; Licht und Projektionsfläche bleiben fest.

```text
Eine einfache Vorführung im Klassenzimmer gestalten. Eine kleine Lampe links leuchtet auf eine senkrechte weiße Projektionsfläche rechts. Dazwischen steht eine einzige lichtundurchlässige quadratische Karte an einem kurzen Griff. Eine feste Kamera von der Seite zeigt Lampe, Karte und Schatten gemeinsam.
00:00–00:05 — Die Ausgangsanordnung halten. Eine erwachsene Hand umfasst den Kartengriff, ohne die Lampe zu verdecken.
00:05–00:10 — Die Karte langsam näher zur Lampe bewegen, entlang der Verbindungslinie zwischen Lampe und Projektionsfläche. Ihr Schatten auf der Fläche wird größer. Lampe und Projektionsfläche bewegen sich nicht.
00:10–00:15 — Anhalten und die neue Anordnung halten. Die Hand hält die Karte ruhig.
SPRECHERTEXT: Auf klarem Deutsch genau sagen: „Das Licht bleibt hier. Wenn wir die Karte näher an das Licht bewegen, wird ihr Schatten größer.“
TON: Leise Klassenzimmergeräusche unter dem Sprechertext; keine Musik.
TEXT: Keiner.
BEIBEHALTEN: Eine Lampe, eine Karte, eine Projektionsfläche, gleichbleibende Helligkeit und ein einziger konsistenter Schatten.
VERMEIDEN: schrumpfenden Schatten während der Bewegung, mehrere Lichtquellen, schwebende Karte, veränderte Projektionsfläche, zusätzliche Beschriftungen, Logos oder Wasserzeichen.
```
